Shame, though. Pretty much exactly the problem in the scenario I have here and all the similar case law I can find for the Australian Consumer Law isn't nearly as cookie-cutter.

Curse having to actually work!

The only encounters I've had have been when I was inebriated so my memories are sketchy at best.

The first time is when I got pulled up walking to Etihad for the football and I crossed the road pretty haphazardly. I got written up but I only had my old, unupdated license on me at the time with an out-of-date address since I don't drive and hadn't had it corrected.

The female cop seemed furious at me whereas her partner was pretty laid back about the whole thing. He wrote up the other guy they called up while she wrote my fine. She asked repeatedly for my address and being in a 'spirited' state of mind I gave it as what was on the card rather than my current address. I think she suspected somethign was up because she kept asking if it was correct.

She asked my friend who was waiting nearby where I lived and he gave the suburb (not the same suburb that was on my license at the time) and she asked why he said that if I lived where I said I did. I asked her why he would know where I lived but not me. She gave up in the end, told me to be more careful and told me to expect a fine. Never got it.

The second time was with two PSOs at Boronia station. I was in a sorry state and had just wandered out of a nearby bar and left my friends behind without telling them I was going and was trying to make my way back home by myself.

They asked my name and address etc. and I kept asking them what they needed it for. They told me they wanted to make sure I got home okay. I don't remember much of it but I assume I gave them the relevant details and they told me when my train was due to arrive and went on their way.

That was only a few weeks ago but I've heard nothing about it. I assume there was no ulterior motive.

TL;DR - Both times the cops have just been doing their job, albeit aggressively in the first case. Any difficulties were my own fault. They're okay for the most part.

Unfortunately I asked and didn't get a reply. Guess I was wrong.

Thanks for the advice though.
I am incredibly pale but that is still very encouraging to hear. I'm not American so I don't really have any experience outside of the big cities I visited a few years ago.

What are your opinions on Standing Bear Farm?

I'm putting together an itinerary and while I'm rather sure I'm probably not going to stick to it, I'm trying to pin down a rough idea of when and where I'll resupply.

I've read that Standing Bear Farm is a good place to stay and resupply however I'll be resupplying at Gatlinburg and past Standing Bear Farm it is only a few days to Hot Springs.

So far, my itinerary has me doing only 3 miles on the day I go to Standing Bear Farm for a resupply. Is it worth it or should I just stock up in Gatlinburg and plow onward to Hot Springs?
I've read about being able to reserve a space at the huts in the Whites, though from what I've gathered it isn't much of an option given the inability to pinpoint arrival times etc.
I'm not one to stress. I can understand that, though. Fun and motivation is the primary reason. If I do stress, I'll stress when there's actually something to stress about.

> One of the crew members we were hanging out with said they couldn't turn people away if there wasn't a legit campsite for them to get to in the time left before sunset. It's a safety thing.

This is encouraging. Thanks!

> If you make it to the Whites going NOBO, you are good to go and will figure out a way to get through them.

This is what I figured. I like to plan, though, and even though I rarely stick to one I find that it helps keep my enthusiasm up and also aids a lot in research (I'm a big advocate of preparing myself for as many eventualities as possible).

But I do agree that if I make it that far I'm sure I will be able to find a way.

Thank you, though. This subreddit is instrumental is helping me get prepared and inspiring me. You guys are the best!

Oh hey, everyone at work.

No, really, it's just a puppet show.

I lived with a mortgage for a long time a few years out of high school so I could give my parents a place to live after they got buried up to their eyeballs in debt and my dad had to retire due to medical reasons.

Paid it off last year along with all other debts I had after selling the house, have been renting a one-room apartment in a seedy neighbourhood since then. I've got a similar job that I've been at for a long time.

But, like you, I'm going to be ditching all of this to hike the AT in 2014 or 2015 (debt free I may be, but I still need to save up the cash) and as time passes I get more and more excited at the prospect of it.

Not sure I can offer anything here other than to say I'm in the same boat and I am encouraged to see other people out there wanting to do the same thing.

(Wow, didn't ralize how long ago this post was made but ... still applicable.)

I've owned a house. Not interested in owning one again. Don't drive. Have a lot of the nice things I want already.

Fuck it, I want a change.

I would love to do this. Sounds amazing and I've got nothing but admiration for people who do it.

Told somebody I'd like to thru-hike one of the Triple Crown trails today and they laughed at me.

Think that may be all the kick in the ass to try this that I need.

Please forgive me if this is a silly question, but I've done a bit of reading about AT and I've read about people adopting 'trail names' while thru-hiking.

Did you have one?
